articles.headline: BofA Delays Fed Rate-Cut Forecast Into 2027
articles.source: TheStreet (citing Bloomberg report of BofA note)
articles.summary: Bank of America Global Research now expects the Federal Reserve to remain on hold for the rest of 2026, shifting its forecast to two quarter-point cuts in July and September 2027. BofA head of U.S. economics Aditya Bhave stated on May 8 that 'the data simply don't warrant cuts this year,' citing core PCE inflation at 3.2% year-over-year and a stronger-than-expected April jobs report of 115,000 nonfarm payrolls added. The Fed held the benchmark federal funds rate steady at 3.50%–3.75% at its April 29 meeting in an unusually divisive 8–4 vote, the closest since 1992. Goldman Sachs separately projects its first rate cut for December 2026, while traders on the CME FedWatch Tool are pricing the next cut for mid-to-late 2027.

articles.headline: Global Net Lease To Acquire Modiv Industrial REIT In $535M Deal
articles.summary: Global Net Lease (NYSE: GNL) announced a $535 million all-stock merger agreement to acquire Modiv Industrial (NYSE: MDV), the only publicly traded REIT exclusively focused on single-tenant industrial manufacturing real estate. Modiv shareholders will receive 1.975 newly issued GNL shares per Modiv share, representing a 17% premium to Modiv's May 1, 2026 closing price of $18.82 per share. Upon closing—expected in Q3 2026 pending Modiv shareholder approval—existing GNL stockholders will own 89% of the combined company. GNL intends to repay Modiv's balance sheet debt and preferred stock using its revolving credit facility and cash on hand; the deal is expected to be immediately 4% accretive to GNL's AFFO per share.

articles.headline: EQT To Spend $1.1B Buying Into Americold Warehouses
articles.summary: Americold Realty Trust (NYSE: COLD) and EQT's Active Core Infrastructure fund announced a $1.3 billion joint venture covering 12 cold storage facilities across the United States, totaling approximately 124 million cubic feet of temperature-controlled capacity and over 400,000 pallet positions. EQT will acquire a 70% interest in the joint venture while Americold retains a 30% equity stake and continues as day-to-day manager; Americold expects to receive approximately $1.1 billion in net cash proceeds to repay outstanding debt. The transaction is expected to close in Q3 2026 subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals. Americold's stock jumped 17% on the announcement; the company had seen its stock fall nearly 70% since 2021 amid oversupply in the cold storage sector.

articles.headline: Inland Empire Industrial Slump Deepens, But Brokers Say Rebound May Be Near
articles.summary: The Inland Empire industrial vacancy rate reached 7.8% in Q1 2026, with negative net absorption of 4.7 million square feet driven by four spaces of 1 million square feet or more that went vacant in the quarter, according to CBRE. Total inventory in the market stands at 660.4 million square feet, with an 8.1% vacancy rate leaving approximately 53.6 million square feet of empty space, per Colliers. New construction deliveries dropped sharply to just 102,000 square feet in Q1 2026, down from nearly 2 million square feet in the same period a year prior. Colliers tracked average asking rents in the Inland Empire West at $1.10 per square foot and IE East at $0.90 per square foot, for a marketwide average of $1.00 per square foot.

articles.headline: Anaheim Industrial Outdoor Storage Site Secures Bridge Loan
articles.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged $26 million in bridge financing for a 7.75-acre industrial outdoor storage facility at 1477 N. Jefferson St. in Anaheim, California, on behalf of borrower North Palisade Partners. The non-recourse, three-year, floating-rate loan covers a Class A property totaling 337,590 square feet at the southwest corner of North Jefferson St. and Orangethorpe Ave. The site is fully leased to a Fortune 100 logistics company that uses the facility as secured parking to support two nearby distribution centers, with 161 trailer parking stalls and two points of ingress and egress. The property is located 1.1 miles from State Route 91 and approximately 33 miles from both the Port of Long Beach and Port of Los Angeles. JLL's team was led by Senior Director Peter Thompson, Associate Kyle White, and Analyst Nick Englhard.

articles.headline: Inland Empire Manufacturing Building Sells to Investor
articles.summary: Proficio Realty LLC acquired a 17,767-square-foot industrial manufacturing building at 255 Glider Circle in Corona, California from Mark J. & Ronda L. Haupert for $5.3 million, or $298 per square foot. The single-story reinforced concrete property, built in 1999, currently houses Elastomer Technologies as its tenant. The transaction was reported by CoStar on May 11, 2026. Full details of the transaction terms are available exclusively to CoStar subscribers.

articles.headline: Top Industrial Leases Recognized for Inland Empire — Q1 2026 CoStar Power Broker Awards
articles.summary: CoStar recognized the top Q1 2026 industrial leases in the Inland Empire market, with prominent deals signed by Tireco, Medline, and Unis negotiated by top dealmakers from CBRE. The CoStar Power Broker Awards evaluate all deals that closed during the previous quarter through CoStar's professional research team. Full details of individual lease sizes, terms, and locations are available exclusively to CoStar subscribers.

articles.headline: Columbia Container Lines Inks 68-Month, $13.6M Lease in Fullerton
articles.summary: The Klabin Company/CORFAC International represented Columbia Container Lines LAX, Inc. in a 68-month lease transaction for a 156,096-square-foot industrial property located at 691-701 Burning Tree Rd. in Fullerton, Orange County. The lease is valued at more than $13.6 million. Tyler Rollema, SIOR, and Matt Stringfellow, SIOR, of The Klabin Company represented Columbia Container Lines, which is relocating and expanding from its prior location. No landlord representative was identified in the public report.

articles.headline: Southern California Landlords Hit With Biggest U.S. Industrial Leasing Drop
articles.summary: Industrial landlords in Southern California's Inland Empire posted one of the steepest quarterly occupancy losses of any U.S. industrial market, with tenants vacating 4 million more square feet than they moved into in Q2 2025, per CoStar data. The Inland Empire's vacancy rate reached a 15-year high of 8.5%, prompting landlords to offer rent concessions, lean into renewals, and market top-tier properties. Nationally, industrial tenants vacated more space than they moved into for the first time in 15 years, pushing the U.S. industrial vacancy rate to 7.5%, its highest level in more than a decade. IDC Logistics recently signed two major leases totaling more than 1.1 million square feet in the Inland Empire, and Dedeaux Properties secured a full-building lease in Fontana with global third-party logistics firm Pilot Air Freight.

articles.headline: FOMC Holds Federal Funds Rate at 3.50%–3.75% in Divisive April Vote
articles.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee voted to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3.5% to 3.75% at its April 29, 2026 meeting, marking the third consecutive meeting at which rates were held unchanged. The 8–4 vote was the most divisive FOMC decision since October 1992, with Governor Miran voting to lower rates by 25 basis points and three other members objecting to language in the statement suggesting the Fed would eventually resume cutting rates. The Committee stated it is 'strongly committed to supporting maximum employment and returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.' Kevin Warsh, President Trump's nominated successor to Chair Jerome Powell, was set for a Senate confirmation appointment on May 15.
